reasoning_summary: Stepwise check. Lines 0003 (4*118/3 = 157.33...) and 0005 (primes strictly between 118 and 157.33 are 127, 131, 137, 139, 149, 151, 157) are correct. All fourteen representations in the eqn block 0008-0048 check out arithmetically: 127 = 4*32-1 = 6*21+1; 131 = 4*33-1 = 6*22-1; 137 = 4*34+1 = 6*23-1; 139 = 4*35-1 = 6*23+1; 149 = 4*37+1 = 6*25-1; 151 = 4*38-1 = 6*25+1; 157 = 4*39+1 = 6*26+1. Line 0055 (4m-1: 127, 131, 139, 151) is correct. Line 0058 FAILS: it lists the primes of the form 4m+1 as 137, 139, 157, but 139 = 4*35-1 (139 mod 4 = 3), and the proof's own line 0027 states 139 = 4*35-1; the prime 149 = 4*37+1, established at line 0033, is omitted. The correct list is 137, 149, 157. This contradicts the immediately preceding lines of the same proof. Separately, and more fundamentally, even if 0058 were corrected the argument would not establish the theorem: it verifies only the single instances n = 118 and n = 117 and offers no argument covering general n >= 118, so lines 0066-0076 do not yield the universally quantified claim.
